== Inukai-be ==

'''Inukai-be''' (犬養部) was a [[Shinabe clans|professional group]] (品部) during the pre-Taika era in Japan, serving the central government through their expertise in the breeding and use of {{ill|Dog|ja|犬|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/dogs|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イヌ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q144}}.

== Origins and Significance of Inukai-be ==

The purposes of dog usage in Inukai-be have traditionally been explained in two ways:

1. For {{ill|Hunting|en|Hunting|qid=Q36963|lt=hunting}}
2. For {{ill|guard|ja|守衛|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/guard duty|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q680928}}

According to the ''{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ar|نيهون شوكي|as|নিহন শ্ব'কি|az|Nihon şoki|bcl|Nihon Shoki|bg|Нихоншоки|ca|Nihon Shoki|cs|Nihonšoki|de|Nihonshoki|el|Νιχόν Σόκι|eo|Nihon Ŝoki|es|Nihonshoki|eu|Nihon Shoki|fa|نیهون شوکی|fi|Nihonshoki|fr|Nihon shoki|gl|Nihon Shoki|he|ניהון שוקי|hi|निहोन शोकी|hr|Nihon Shoki|hu|Nihonsoki|id|Nihon Shoki|it|Nihon shoki|ja|日本書紀|jv|Nihon Shoki|ko|일본서기|la|Nihon Shoki|mk|Нихон шоки|ms|Nihon Shoki|my|နိဟွန်းရှောခိ|nl|Nihon Shoki|no|Nihonshoki|oc|Nihon shoki|pl|Nihon-shoki|pt|Nihon Shoki|rsk|Нихон Шоки|ru|Нихон сёки|sco|Nihon Shoki|sh|Nihon Shoki|simple|Nihon Shoki|sl|Nihon Šoki|sq|Nihon Shoki|sr|Нихон шоки|sv|Nihonshoki|ta|நிஹான் ஷோகி|th|นิฮงโชกิ|tl|Nihon Shoki|tr|Nihon Shoki|uk|Ніхон Сьокі|uz|Nihon shoki|vi|Nhật Bản thư kỷ|zh|日本書紀|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún Su-kì|zh_yue|日本書紀|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}'', Inukai-be was established in August of the second year of Emperor Ankan's reign (538), following the mass establishment of {{ill|Miyake|ja|屯倉|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyake|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11465761}} (imperial granaries) in May of the same year. Given the close timing of these events and the frequent proximity of place names like "Miyake" and "Inukai," it is widely believed that Inukai-be was tasked with guarding the Miyake using dogs.

While the exact founding period of Inukai-be remains uncertain, the presence of a place named "Inukai" at the site of Emperor Ankan's former residence, {{ill|Magari no Kanahashi Palace|ja|勾金橋宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagamihashi Palace|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q126889667}}, suggests its origins may date back to the first half of the 6th century. The frequent records of Miyake establishment in the ''Nihon Shoki'' from Emperor Ankan's era onward imply that the development of Miyake was closely linked to the establishment of Inukai-be. Moreover, the widespread expansion of Miyake is believed to have laid the groundwork for the later {{ill|provincial administrative system|ja|国・郡・里制}}.

== Leaders of Inukai-be ==

Historical records such as the ''Nihon Shoki'' and the ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku|qid=Q1045362|lt=Shinsen Shōjiroku}}'' mention several clans that led Inukai-be, known as {{ill|Tomonomiyatsuko|ja|伴造|lt=Tomo no Miyatsuko}}:

* {{ill|Agata no Inukai clan|ja|県犬養氏|ru|Агата-Инукаи|uk|Аґата-Інуакаї|qid=Q11582689}}
* {{ill|Ama Inukai no Muraji|ja|海犬養連|qid=DELETED_QID}}
* {{ill|Waka Inukai no Muraji|ja|若犬養連|qid=DELETED_QID}}
* {{ill|Azumi Inukai no Muraji|ja|阿曇犬養連|qid=DELETED_QID}}
* Kara Inukai no Muraji (辛犬養連)
* Ata Mite Inukai (阿多御手犬養)

While the title "Inukai no Muraji" without a prefix also appears in the ''Nihon Shoki'', it is likely due to missing clan names. Among these, Agata no Inukai, Ama Inukai, and Waka Inukai are considered prominent high-Ranking Tomo no Miyatsuko.

Some theories classify these clans as follows:

* Ama Inukai, Waka Inukai, Azumi Inukai, and Kara Inukai: associated with maritime clans (海神族系)
* Ata Mite Inukai: related to the {{ill|Hayato people|de|Hayato (Volk)|fa|مردم هایاتو|fr|Hayato|id|Suku Hayato|ja|隼人|ko|하야토|ru|Хаято|uk|Хаято|zh|隼人|zh_min_nan|Hayato|qid=Q1151764|lt=Hayato people}} lineage
* Agata no Inukai: linked to the {{ill|Yamatsumi clan|ja|山祇族}}

Notably, the Agata no Inukai clan produced influential figures during the Asuka to mid-Nara periods, such as:

* {{ill|Agata no Inukai no Michiyo|fa|آگاتا نو انوکای نو میچیو|ja|県犬養三千代|no|Agata no Inukai no Michiyo|ru|Агата-Инукаи-но Митиё|uk|Аґата-Інуакаї но Мітійо|zh|縣犬養三千代|qid=Q11582685|lt=Agata no Inukai no Michiyo}} – wife of {{ill|Fujiwara no Fuhito|ca|Fujiwara no Fuhito|de|Fujiwara no Fuhito|es|Fujiwara no Fuhito|fa|فوجیوارا نو فوهیتو|fr|Fujiwara no Fuhito|hr|Fujiwara no Fuhito|id|Fujiwara no Fuhito|it|Fujiwara no Fuhito|ja|藤原不比等|ko|후지와라노 후히토|nl|Fujiwara no Fuhito|pl|Fuhito Fujiwara|pt|Fujiwara no Fuhito|ru|Фудзивара-но Фухито|sh|Fujiwara no Fuhito|th|ฟูจิวาระ โนะ ฟูฮิโตะ|tr|Fujiwara no Fuhito|uk|Фудзівара но Фухіто|vi|Fujiwara no Fuhito|zh|藤原不比等|zh_min_nan|Huziwara no Huhito|qid=Q177517|lt=Fujiwara no Fuhito}} and mother of {{ill|Empress Kōmyō|de|Kōmyō (Kaiserin)|es|Emperatriz Kōmyō|fa|امپراتریس کومیو|fi|Kōmyō (keisarinna)|fr|Kōmyō (impératrice)|hi|साम्राज्ञी कोमियो|id|Permaisuri Kōmyō|ja|光明皇后|ko|고묘 황후|ru|Императрица Комё|sv|Kōmyō|th|จักรพรรดินีโคเมียว|vi|Hoàng hậu Kōmyō|zh|光明皇后|qid=Q837932|lt=Fujiwara no Kōmyō}} and {{ill|Tachibana no Moroe|fa|تاچیبانا نو موروئه|ff|Tachibana no Moroe|fr|Tachibana no Moroe|ja|橘諸兄|pl|Tachibana no Moroe|pt|Tachibana no Moroe|sh|Tachibana no Moroe|uk|Татібана но Морое|vi|Tachibana no Moroe|zh|橘诸兄|qid=Q3135863|lt=Tachibana no Moroe}}
* {{ill|Agatainukai no Hirotoji|ja|県犬養広刀自|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Agata no Inukai no Hirotoji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11582687}} – mother of Prince Asaka, son of Emperor Shōmu

== Later History of Inukai-be ==

Initially focused on guarding Miyake, the Inukai-be eventually transitioned away from dog handling. They leveraged the martial skills honed through their security roles to evolve into a military clan. This shift is evidenced by the participation of Inukai clan members in the {{ill|Isshi incident|en|Isshi incident|qid=Q1062771|lt=Isshi Incident}}—the coup that led to the assassination of {{ill|Soga no Iruka|en|Soga no Iruka|qid=Q736621|lt=Soga no Iruka}}—including {{ill|Amanoinukai no Katsumaro|ja|海犬養勝麻呂|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ama Inukai no Katsumaro|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q51915273}} and {{ill|Katsuragi no Wakainukai no Amita|ja|葛城稚犬養網田|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katsuragi Waka Inukai no Amida|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q51914871}}.
